newsitem.title: USA: ATHLETICS-MICHAEL JOHNSON STILL INJURED, PULLS OUT OF STUTTGART.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-MICHAEL JOHNSON STILL INJURED, PULLS OUT OF STUTTGART.

text.p: Double Olympic champion Michael Johnson has not completely recovered from back and leg problems and pulled out Wednesday from Sunday's planned 400 metres race in Stuttgart, his coach said.

Unless the world and Olympic 200 and 400 metres champion receives a wild card to next month's world championships, he will not compete again until the August 13 Zurich grand prix meeting, Clyde Hart said in a telephone interview from his home in Waco, Texas.

Johnson, who missed the U.S. championships because of the injuries, can compete in the August 1-10 world championships in Athens only if the International Amateur Athletic Federation grants him a wild card entry.
The IAAF is expected to decide before Monday whether to extend special invitations to Johnson and other defending world champions who might otherwise miss the meeting.
"I'm gearing for Zurich and if the world championships are a possibility, we will approach that and see if that's what we want to do," Hart, Johnson's long-time trainer, said.
"He can probably run and do well (now) but we don't want to have another setback," Hart said. "He's not 100 percent."

Johnson severely pulled his left quadriceps in a June 1 loss to Canadian 100 metres world record holder Donovan Bailey in their 150 metres showdown, then stunningly faded to fifth in his first race back on June 25 in Paris.
The loss snapped an eight-year 400 metres winning streak for Johnson, and he promptly returned home to Texas for more training.
"His workouts are going well," said Hart, "but during these practice sessions he's had some recurring problems that make us realise that it's not 100 percent, and he's getting treatment."
Hart said Johnson still had some swelling in his left leg and his back was causing what the coach described as "referred pain in his leg."
"About every third or fourth day there would be recurring soreness," Hart said.
Johnson had similar problems with his back in the Olympics and had to get it realigned between his 200 metres semifinal and world-record final, Hart said.
"He could go over and run very well in Europe now," Hart added. "But we don't want to run 'very well.' We want to do something special."
